The people in Isaiah are nose blind to their own sin. And friends, I'd love to tell you, I'd love to give you this false comfort and say, but that was just them. It's definitely not you. That's not why Isaiah exists.
God's holiness is telling us, is assigning meaning to what he sees. He is seeing through the lens, if you will, of his holiness.
By definition, true victims are often invisible. In some cases, the whole, a whole system, a whole culture gets to, gets built to make the victims invisible.
Spurgeon said, I believe that one reason why the church of God at this present moment has so little influence over the world is because the world has so much influence over the church.

When you understand how firmly God stands with the victim and you're in that position, if you have the love of Christ inside of you, you will actively intercede for your enemies because you understand what's coming for them.

external.text: God doesn't judge by appearances. A work that looks good on the outside doesn't fool him. So his knowledge, and therefore his judgment, works on a completely different level from ours. Because his understanding is perfect, God looks through the veil and sees the heap of filth hidden in the soul. He sees that each act— he sees what each act really is and the motive behind it. And he judges things as they are, not as they look. Disguises can't deceive him since he knows them long before they were woven. He reaches into the deepest and most tangled wills, and every hidden motive is laid bare, laid open before him. Each action is bare on the outside and open on the inside. Everything is as clear to him as if our bodies were made of glass. So if we hold anything back in secret, he will surely call us to account.
external.author: Stephen Charnock

lines.text: If no one was able to open this scroll, then all suffering, pain, and sorrow that God's people face in this life would be meaningless.
He conquered our greatest enemies sin and death through His sacrificial death on the cross.
In Christ, you are a beloved child of God. You are more loved than you'll ever know, and that will never change.

If there was no one worthy to open the scroll, then history would not be governed for the good of the church. And if history is not being governed for the good of the church, then prayer itself will be meaningless and useless.
Christ will have what he paid for in full.
We were born slaves to sin. And because of our sin, we deserve death and everlasting punishment.

sermons.title: Alive in Christ, Nailed To The Cross

lines.text: Christ is not a starter kit. If there is a system that wants Jesus to step aside so that they can actually— that system can actually get to your real problem, well, that system just told you what it really thinks about Jesus Christ.

The Savior who brought you in is the Savior who carries you through. When you received Christ, you received a person, Christ Jesus the Lord. You didn't sign up for a method that you could eventually master and then leave behind.
You are in Christ, you are joined to the living Lord. You're not reaching through Christ to some higher spiritual power.
Staying put in Christ, it doesn't mean that we stand still. Roots don't stand still. They go deep, they draw life, and then buildings don't stay still.
Our growth and healing in the Christian life comes From our union with a crucified and risen Christ.

You can feel at the end of yourself. You can feel broken. You can feel empty and still have a complete Savior. It's just that in that moment, we know what to do with our brokenness. We know what to do with our emptiness. We take it to the one who is full, and in him we get full.
